description: A D type flip flop: it reads the level at D on each rising clock edge and holds it at the outputs, working as a sample and hold for gates

inputs.text: The level captured at the next rising edge at CLOCK; over 2V counts as high, and it counts as low again below 0.1V
Each rising edge over 2V here copies the level at D to the Q output and its inverse to the NOT Q output, as long as the flip flop is enabled
With nothing patched here, the flip flop is clocked at all times; with a cable patched, a gate over 2V must be present here for a clock edge to be acted on

outputs.text: Holds 10V or 0V, the level read at D on the last rising clock edge
Holds the inverse of the level read at D on the last rising clock edge: 0V when that was high, 10V when it was low
